title: A Vow for the Harbor
premise: Orsen Vane inherited her uncle's failing vineyard along with a mountain of debt and a decade of anonymous letters that kept the creditors at bay—letters she never answered because answering meant admitting how far she'd fallen. When Mara Quill, the quiet woman who wrote them, moves into the cottage next door, Orsen must confront the stranger who knew her better than anyone, and the truth that her uncle's death was no accident. As the last ferry of the season approaches, Orsen and Mara untangle loyalty, guilt, and a cover-up the whole harbor town protected, forcing Orsen to forgive herself before she can choose a future. The story ends with Orsen testifying to the truth, the vineyard saved by the community she finally let in, and Orsen and Mara boarding the ferry together—not leaving, but returning.
about_author: Ivo Montrose is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent years cataloguing letters recovered from coastal estates. They write romances about people who mistake silence for safety, and live within sight of a ferry terminal they refuse to stop watching.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unsent Things
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She surveys the dying vineyard, dodges a creditor's call, and rereads one of the anonymous letters that has quietly paid her bills for ten years. Emotional beat: shame disguised as independence; she almost burns the letter but can't.

chapters.title: A Moving Truck at the Property Line
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A woman unloads boxes into the derelict cottage next door—the first neighbor the vineyard road has had in years. Their first exchange is prickly, practical, and oddly familiar. Beat: unease flickering into curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Remembers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara unpacks deliberately, revealing to the reader (not Orsen) that she wrote the letters, and recalls why she stopped. Beat: longing tempered by fear of being recognized.

chapters.title: Bottles and Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A bank notice gives her ninety days. She attempts a harvest with hired help she can't afford and swallows her pride enough to accept Mara's offer of labor. Beat: grudging alliance over bruised fruit.

chapters.title: The Handwriting on the Envelope
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Sorting old paperwork, Orsen recognizes Mara's handwriting on a shipping label—and goes cold. She says nothing, but begins testing her. Beat: suspicion curdling the new warmth.

chapters.title: Salt and Small Confessions
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Over shared dinner, Mara deflects questions about her past while learning how alone Orsen truly is. She nearly confesses, then doesn't. Beat: intimacy built on an omission.

chapters.title: The Uncle's Locked Shed
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen finds her uncle's shed padlocked from the inside with records missing, and a neighbor's offhand comment suggests the town knows more about his death than she does. Beat: grief sharpening into doubt.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flashback chapter: how Mara came to write the letters after witnessing something at the vineyard the night Orsen's uncle died. Beat: guilt as devotion; love born from complicity.

chapters.title: An Accusation at the Dock
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The creditor accuses Orsen of fraud, claiming the anonymous payments were laundered money. Public humiliation at the ferry dock; Mara defends her fiercely. Beat: Orsen realizes someone is protecting her—and lying for her.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Dual tension scene, mostly Orsen's POV. Orsen corners Mara among the barrels: 'You wrote them.' Mara admits it—but not why. Beat: betrayal and relief colliding; the friendship fractures.

chapters.title: What I Saw That Night
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara tells the partial truth: she saw Orsen's uncle alive after the 'accident,' and someone powerful made sure the record said otherwise. She stayed silent to protect Orsen. Beat: the mystery widens; trust tentatively rebuilt.

chapters.title: The Town That Kept the Secret
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen interviews harbor locals and hits a wall of polite silence—until the old ferry captain hints her uncle was blackmailing someone. Beat: loneliness of being lied to by an entire community.

chapters.title: Harvest Under Threat
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Sabotage: equipment destroyed days before the make-or-break harvest. Mara works beside her through the night without being asked. Beat: love surfacing in action before either names it.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. After the harvest, wine-stained and exhausted, Orsen and Mara nearly kiss—then Orsen pulls back, unable to be close to someone who still holds secrets. Beat: yearning defeated by unfinished truth.

chapters.title: The Ferry Captain's Ledger
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The captain gives Orsen her uncle's confiscated ledger, naming the town's beloved patriarch as the man her uncle was blackmailing—and the likely killer. Beat: dread; justice now has a face she knows.

chapters.title: A Vow Reconsidered
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara reveals her final secret: she took money from the patriarch years ago to stay silent, believing she was protecting Orsen from a dangerous truth. Orsen walks out. Beat: the vow of protection revealed as its own betrayal.

chapters.title: Days Without Neighbors
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Mara prepares to leave on the last ferry. Orsen, alone with the ledger and her uncle's debts, realizes her anger is really at herself—for accepting help she never questioned. Beat: the turn inward; forgiveness of self begins.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen visits her uncle's grave and admits aloud that she let the letters buy her silence too—that invisibility was her choice. She decides to testify. Beat: catharsis; agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: Testimony at the Harbor Hall
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with Mara present. Orsen presents the ledger publicly; the town's protective lie collapses; the patriarch is arrested. Mara publicly takes responsibility for her bought silence. Beat: climax; truth costing everything and freeing everyone.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the dock, Mara boards to settle affairs elsewhere; Orsen lets her go without begging, a first act of faith. Beat: bittersweet suspension; love proven by release rather than pursuit.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Letter
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Weeks later, the community rallies to save the vineyard, and a letter arrives—signed this time. It contains a return ticket and a question. Beat: hope grounded in honesty.

chapters.title: Returning Water
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Spring planting; Mara returns on the season's first ferry. They plant new vines together, having chosen each other with full knowledge. Final beat: second chances aren't timing—they're courage; the harbor keeps what is honestly given.
